assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Precipitate
items.clue: An insoluble solid formed when two solutions are mixed.

items.label: Orange-red flame colour
items.clue: The flame colour produced by calcium compounds in a flame test.

items.label: Flame emission spectroscopy
items.clue: An instrumental method used to analyse metal ions in solutions.

items.label: Lilac flame colour
items.clue: The flame colour produced by potassium compounds in a flame test.

questions.stem: Sodium hydroxide solution is added to a solution of an unknown salt and a precipitate forms. Which ion in the salt does this test identify?

options.text: the negative ion in the salt, its anion
the hydroxide ion from the sodium hydroxide
the positive metal ion in the salt, its cation
both of the ions in the salt at one time

questions.explanation: Sodium hydroxide solution can be used to identify some metal ions (cations).

questions.stem: Dilute hydrochloric acid is added to a white solid that is thought to be a carbonate. What is seen, and what gas is given off?

options.text: It fizzes, giving off carbon dioxide gas.
It fizzes, giving off hydrogen gas.
It fizzes, giving off oxygen gas.
It dissolves quietly, giving off no gas.

questions.explanation: Carbonates react with dilute acids to form carbon dioxide gas.

questions.stem: Dilute nitric acid and then silver nitrate solution are added to a solution of an unknown halide. A cream precipitate forms. What does the solution contain?

options.text: The unknown solution contains chloride ions.
The unknown solution contains carbonate ions.
The unknown solution contains bromide ions.
The unknown solution contains iodide ions.

questions.stem: A student wants to show that a solution contains sulfate ions. What should be added, and what is a positive result?

options.text: dilute nitric acid, then silver nitrate solution: a white precipitate
dilute hydrochloric acid, then barium chloride solution: a white precipitate
dilute hydrochloric acid, then sodium hydroxide: a white precipitate
barium chloride solution alone: a cream coloured precipitate

questions.explanation: Sulfate ions in solution produce a white precipitate with barium chloride solution in the presence of dilute hydrochloric acid.

questions.stem: The specification describes instrumental methods of analysis. Which three words does it use?

options.text: accurate, sensitive and rapid
accurate and sensitive, but slow
cheap, simple and easy to carry
accurate, but far too slow to use.

questions.explanation: Instrumental methods are accurate, sensitive and rapid.

questions.stem: Flame emission spectroscopy is an instrumental method. What is it used to analyse?

options.text: the non-metal ions present in solids
the non-metal ions dissolved in a solution
the mass of a solid sample taken
the metal ions present in solutions

questions.explanation: Flame emission spectroscopy is used to analyse metal ions in solutions.

questions.stem: How did algae and plants change the percentage of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere?

options.text: They increased it, as photosynthesis produces it
They had no effect, as they only ever produce oxygen
They decreased it, taking in only that one gas
They decreased it, as photosynthesis uses it up

questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a reactant in photosynthesis, so algae and plants decreased the percentage of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere.

questions.stem: Sodium hydroxide solution is added, a few drops at a time, to separate solutions of aluminium ions, calcium ions and magnesium ions. What is seen in each tube?

options.text: A white precipitate forms in two of the tubes.
A coloured precipitate forms in each tube.
A white precipitate forms in one tube only.
A white precipitate forms in all three tubes.

questions.explanation: Solutions of aluminium, calcium and magnesium ions form white precipitates when sodium hydroxide solution is added.

questions.stem: The gas given off when a carbonate reacts with a dilute acid is bubbled through limewater. What is the positive result?

options.text: The limewater relights a glowing splint.
The limewater turns cloudy, or milky.
The limewater turns a bright blue.
The limewater becomes colourless.

questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide can be identified with limewater, which turns cloudy.

questions.stem: A solution is acidified with dilute nitric acid and silver nitrate solution is added. A yellow precipitate forms. Which ion is present?

options.text: the bromide ion, Br-
the chloride ion, Cl-
the sulfate ion, SO4 2-
the iodide ion, I-

questions.stem: Barium chloride solution is added to a solution in the presence of dilute hydrochloric acid, and a white precipitate forms. What does this show?

options.text: Chloride ions are present in this solution.
Carbonate ions are present in solution.
Sulfate ions are present in the solution.
Barium ions are present in solution.

questions.explanation: The white precipitate is barium sulfate, so sulfate ions are present.

questions.stem: Give one advantage of using an instrumental method instead of the chemical tests in this specification.

options.text: It can be used without taking a sample at all.
It gives a result that never needs any checking.
It can detect a very small amount of a substance quickly.
It is always cheaper than a simple chemical test.

questions.explanation: Instrumental methods are accurate, sensitive and rapid.
